function.description: Executes a given command using the os.system() function specifically for Windows operating systems. For multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For complex tasks, create and run a .bat file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The Windows command line instruction(s) to be executed. Use '&&' between commands for multiple instructions. For complex sequences, encapsulate the logic within a .bat file and provide the execution command here.

message.reasoning: The user says "start Docker on window using docker start." They want to start Docker on Windows using docker start. But docker start is used to start containers, not the Docker daemon. To start Docker service, you need to start Docker Desktop or the Docker Engine service. On Windows, you can use "net start com.docker.service" or "Start-Service Docker". Or if using Docker Desktop, you can launch the application. The user might want to start Docker engine via command line. We can use PowerShell: Start-Service Docker. Or use "sc start Docker". Or "docker start" is wrong. So we should explain that docker start starts containers, not the Docker daemon. To start Docker service, use "Start-Service Docker" or "net start com.docker.service". Provide command. Also mention that you need admin privileges. Use the function to execute command. Let's propose "Start-Service Docker" or "net start com.docker.service". We'll use cmd_controller_execute with command "net start com.docker.service". That will start the Docker service. Alternatively, "Start-Service Docker" in PowerShell. We'll use cmd_controller_execute.
